outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED. tests/test_build_shop.py: a new section after the last existing case block (nothing added before an existing case; one stage line appended after escblock5 in _cases; a --tripwire-pattern flag in __main__ that prints the input_match line to paste). TRIPWIRE_PARTS is a table of (name, regex text, one sentence) rows: escaped, dq, sq, passed, separator, blank, start, words, git, arg, globals, end, before, rest, and one row per destructive spelling (checkout, checkout-index, switch, restore, restore-worktree, reset, clean, stash), then verb and tripwire. A row names others as %(name)s; tripwire_pattern() resolves them. Each row holding a repeated group argues in its sentence why no two alternatives start on the same character, or where two do (a keyword and an assignment both start on a letter; -C and a long option both start on a dash) where they part. TRIPWIRE_KINDS, TRIPWIRE_TWIN, TRIPWIRE_UNITS (200*2**k, k<3), TRIPWIRE_POWER (1.5), TRIPWIRE_FLOOR, TRIPWIRE_CEILING (0.25 s per match at the longest), TRIPWIRE_DEADLINE (10 s per child), and two timing children (python -I -S -c, node -e) reading a job file. Each child times the lengths interleaved by round (at least 3 rounds, until 0.05 s spent, at most 40) and keeps the least time per length. Per kind and twin, the python and node children start together and each is killed at the deadline; a kill is a failure. WHERE THE PARTS LIVE AND WHY: in the suite, not in a shipped .py. The harness reads only the assembled string in case.yaml; the parts are how the pattern is maintained and argued, and the suite is where the argument is checked. A shipped module would owe a suite, a layer row and a build-guide section for code nothing shipped calls. plugins/audit/evals/guard-stop/case.yaml: input_match is now the assembled string (2048 characters; HEAD's was 1734). What it reads, changed: the double-quoted argument reads a JSON escape as one token and a shell backslash as escaping the next token, so an escaped quote inside it can no longer end it early (the old body's `\\\\\\"` and `\\[^"]` alternatives overlapped). Outside quotes a shell backslash escapes the next character (an escaped quote opens nothing; an escaped ; & | ends nothing; a backslash-newline is no line break). The blanks after a separator and after a prefix word may hold a backslash-newline, so `\<newline>git reset --hard` and `A=b \<newline>git stash` stay counted. A single-quoted argument in argument position now admits a double quote inside it, as the passed-over form already did. Header: the false sentence 'a quoted argument holding an escaped quote, which can end the argument early' is removed. Added: the backslash reading, and a paragraph stating the property, what holds it (the parts in the suite, esc51 equality, the timing cases with the bound names) and the engines (Python's re always, node when on PATH, each run printing which). CHANGELOG.md: the existing Unreleased/Added tripwire bullet gains the same, naming the bounds by constant. KEPT: every GIT_DESTRUCTIVE spelling counted and no GIT_HARMLESS string counted, in either key order with DESCRIBED (esc29/30/41/42/43 green). Old-not-new: harmless by the shell (`echo .py --staged\;git clean -fd`, a continuation joining git into another command's arguments, or text after a quote left unpaired). Script: SP/sg1.28/proto.py.
